title: Introduction To Machine Learning, Spring 2016
description: | **Overview**  Machine learning is an exciting and fast-moving field of computer science with many recent consumer applications (e.g., Microsoft Kinect, Google Translate, Iphone's Siri, digital camera face detection, Netflix recommendations, Google news) and applications within the sciences and medicine (e.g., predicting protein-protein interactions, species modeling, detecting tumors, personalized medicine). In this undergraduate-level class, students will learn about the theoretical foundations of machine learning and how to apply machine learning to solve new problems. David Sontag |  | dsontag {@ | at} cs.nyu.edu | | **TA**: |  | Kevin Jiao |  | jj1745 {@ | at} nyu.edu | | **Graders:** |  | Alexandre Sablayrolles |  | sla382 {@ | at} nyu.edu | |  |  | Yijun Xiao |  | ryjxiao {@ | at} nyu.edu |  Office hours (David): Tuesdays 4:30-5:30pm. Linear algebra (MATH-UA 140) is strongly recommended as a pre-requisite, and knowledge of multivariable calculus will be helpful. Bishop's book is easier to read, whereas Murphy's book has more depth and coverage (and is up to date).
